page.layout: One printed page. Running head "ITALIA." at top centre; page number 79 at top right. Main text in one column of verse, with a heading-like line "Pæstum oppidum Campaniæ." in the middle. Marginal notes in the right margin, beside the verse lines.

p.i: Quis nam mutato tantùm nunc tempore credat?
Luxus, & infanis nutrita ignauia lustris,
Consumptúsque pudor peccando, vnisque relictus
Diuitiys probrosus honor, lacerabat hiantem
Desidia populum, ac resolutam legibus vrbem.
Insuper exitio truculenta superbia agebat.
Nec vitiys deerant vires: non largior vlli
Ausonia populos (fictum fortuna fouebat)
Auriqué argentique modus, madefacta veneno
Assyrio, manibus vestis, medióque dierum
Regales epula, atque ortu conuiuia solis
Deprensa, & nulla macula non illita vita.
Tum populo sauí patres, plebésque senatus
Inuidia lacera, & collidens dissona corda
Seditio: sed enim interea temeraria pubes
Delicta augebat, pollutior ipsa senectus.
Nec quos vile genus, despectáque lucis origo
Fœdabat, sperare sibi & deposcere primi
Deerant imperio, ac patria pereuntis habenas.
Quinetiam exhilarare viris conuiuia cade
Mos olim, & miscere epulis spectacula dira,
Certantum ferro sape, & super ipsa cadentum
Pocula respersis non parco sanguine mensis.
Circum aderant mensæ egregia, dapibúsque referta,
Qualibus accubuit Capua dux luscus: & ipsi
Accubuere olim qui Ancylia sacra tenebant.
Forsitan, & pingues hortos, qua cura colendi
Ornaret, canerem, bisque rosaria Pæsti.
Nec Babylon æstus, nec frigora Pontus habebit,
Calibáque Pæstanas vincet odore rosas.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right: "Capua olim dicitissima.", "Deliciæ & mores Capuanorum corruptissimi.", "Palinge. in Geminu.", "Virg. Georg. lib.4.", "Ouid. de Ponto lib.1." Some marginal text is small and partly illegible; the reading of "Palinge. in Geminu." and "Ouid. de Ponto" is uncertain. Several verse lines have faint ink; the words "ortu", "Calibáque" and "Pæstanas" are doubtful.
